title: papagorgio23-FantasyFootball
universal_lens: The optimization of discrete roster configurations under strict budgetary and positional constraints constitutes a high-dimensional combinatorial selection problem. Mathematically, this maps to an Integer Linear Programming (ILP) formulation, where the objective is maximizing expected value subject to linear equality and inequality constraints, forming the foundational kernel for constrained resource allocation. Linear programming formulation of fantasy football lineup optimization under resource constraints.
gsi_mapping: Within GSI, the deterministic objective vector f is replaced by a posterior predictive distribution derived from hierarchical Bayesian player models. Conformal inference bounds are applied to the projected scores, transforming the classical LP into a robust chance-constrained optimization that explicitly accounts for epistemic uncertainty in weekly performance projections. Bayesian belief updates on player performance using constrained optimization via Rglpk_solve_LP for lineup selection.
gse_mapping: GSE treats the lineup optimizer as a dynamic state-transition engine. The binary selection vector x represents a situational action mapping current market prices to optimal tactical deployments. The constraint matrix A dynamically adapts to real-time injury reports and defensive matchups, ensuring valid transitions between roster states. Situational reasoning engine evaluates state transitions in roster construction through dual solution vectors and status flags.
